author: Fabri (from Kuraishi and Chandra)
asr_identification: hill with the caves reached by the Bimbisara road, Rajgir, Patna district
evidence: caves cleared 1931-32; shellac seals with a Buddha among stupas and a medieval inscription; small seated stone Buddha found in a cave the next year; Bimbisara road repaired
quote: repairs have been done among others to the famous ancient road of King Bimbisara leading up to the caves on the Gridhrakiija Hill, (Plate XIU, a.) While clearing these caves during 1931-32, Mr H. KvRaAIsHi found a few shellac seals hearing a figure of the Buddha in the centre with numerous sftipas represented sround him
note: Conservation summary, but the finds show Buddhist worship at the caves on the hill now called Gridhrakuta (the road = Xuanzang's road built by Bimbisara). Takes the identification as given; agrees with Mizutani (Gridhrakuta at Rajgir). Unlike Beglar (ASR 08), places the Gridhrakuta at the caves reached by the Bimbisara road. Same passage also has the Maniyar Math image inscribed "Vipula" (see 487)

author: Chakravarti
asr_identification: Vipula, one of the five hills round old Rajagriha (Girivraja), Rajgir, Patna district
evidence: Kushana-period inscription "parvato Vipula / raja-ganika" on a fragmentary image pedestal from the Maniyar Math area (1932-33)
quote: (1) parvato Vupula … In all probability, this piece of seulpture was dedicated to a shrine existing on the Vipula Hill. … The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsane also mentions it by name, and places it to the west of the north gate of the old Réjagriha, But this is the first epigraphical record found to contain the name of this hill.
note: First inscription naming Vipula, but found at Maniyar Math, not on the hill, so it does not fix which hill is Vipula. Chakravarti follows the text (W of the N gate); Mizutani puts Vipula E of the N gate, with Vaibhara on the W. Cunningham (ASR 01) also has Vipulagiri at Rajgir

author: Chandra; N. G. Majumdar
asr_identification: Gridhrakuta hill with the Bimbisara road, old caves and a summit shrine, Rajgir; Mahasthan (Mahasthangarh), Bogra district
evidence: clearance on the Gridhrakuta found traces of a small cave c. 30 ft below and W of the main shrine on the summit, with signs of other shrines E of it; Bimbisara road and old caves cleared
quote: the Gridhrakuta hills where the Bimbisàra road and the old caves are situated … at the Gridhrakuta area on top of the hills traces of a small cave which still requires further exposure. This cave is situated about 30 feet below and on the west side of the main shrine situated on the top of the hills … the ancient capital of Pundravardhana, in Bogra District
note: Rajgir conservation report (Chandra), and Majumdar's Bengal exploration (excavation of Medh mound near Mahasthan). The summit shrine and caves match Xuanzang's brick vihara on the peak and the caves near it (09.02.10). Agrees with Mizutani for both places

author: Chakravarti
asr_identification: Begram at the confluence of the Ghorband and Panjshir rivers (Foucher); Nalanda monastery site 11, Baragaon
evidence: Kharoshthi inscription on a bas-relief from Begram (Konow), the first found near Kapisi; clay sealings from Monastery 11 at Nalanda with the legend Sri-Nalanda-mahavihare Arya-bhikshu-sanghasya
quote: Begram is situated on the confluence cf the Ghorband and Panjshir rivers and has been identified by Prof. Foucher … Some other seals contain the usual legend &n-Nàlanda … mahaviharé Arya-bhikshu-saighasya or Sri-sanghasya
note: Both agree with Mizutani (Kapisi = Begram basin at the Panjshir-Ghorband confluence; Nalanda = Baragaon ruins); the monastery seals confirm Cunningham's Baragaon. Epigraphy summary, reported without argument

author: Nazim
asr_identification: Gridhrakuta hill, Rajgir, Patna district: two brick stupas half way up the Bimbisara road; brick shrine on the summit; caves near the top
evidence: remains of two ancient brick stupas in the middle of the Bimbisara road half way up cleared; summit brick shrine exposed, with inscribed clay sealings of the Eight Buddhas, beads and a red-stone Buddha in dharmacakra-mudra; traces of shrines and a stone-paved path E and S of the caves
quote: About half way up the hill, remains of a couple of ancient brick stupas in the middle of the road were cleared of debris … Exposing the brick shrine situated on the summit of the hill, a few inscribed clay sealings ^Yith impressions of the Eight Buddhas
note: new: the two small stupas on Bimbisara's road up the Gridhrakuta (where the king dismounted, and where he sent back the crowd) are not in the table; the two brick stupas half way up the road match them. Summit brick shrine = the vihara on the peak (09.02.10). Agrees with Mizutani. Same span: Nalanda Chaitya site 13 (Hiuen Tsang cited only for praise of the buildings), Maniyar Math (Mani-naga inscriptions), Nandangarh and Mahasthan excavations (no bearing on Xiyu ji places)
